sections.h2: Who bills and assesses property tax in Old Bridge, NJ?
sections.html:
Old Bridge Township has its own Tax Assessor and its own Tax Collection office, and both sit in the township's government offices. The assessor values each parcel. The collector bills and takes payment at (732) 721-5600, extension 2999. The township belongs to Middlesex County, which means value disputes are heard in New Brunswick.

The township runs an online account system where owners can see current-year and prior-year tax details, confirm that a payment arrived, and pay by bank account or card. The system's help page notes that nominal fees apply to online payments. For the fourth quarter of 2025 the collector kept weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. and added a Saturday session on November 8, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. To view a balance online, create a login with the Web Login ID printed on the latest bill. An owner who cannot find the bill can email the collection office to get the ID.

sections.h2: What is Old Bridge Township like?
sections.html:
Old Bridge spreads over 38.18 square miles of land in the Raritan Valley, facing Staten Island across Raritan Bay and roughly 25 miles from New York City. Its 2020 count was 66,876 people; the 2025 estimate of 70,228 is a 5.0% rise. Do not confuse that with the Old Bridge census-designated place, a smaller area of 27,210 people in 2020 inside the township's borders.

The township was Madison Township from 1869 until voters approved the new name in a 1975 referendum, 7,150 to 4,888. It has no single downtown. Instead it is a set of communities: Laurence Harbor, Madison Park, Brownville, Parlin, Cheesequake and the Old Bridge center, with ZIP codes 08857, 08859, 08879 and 07735. Cheesequake Creek, the South River and Matchaponix Brook drain the township.

Survey data for 2020 to 2024 shows 70.4% of homes owner-occupied, a typical home value of $461,000 and a typical household income of $104,587, higher than in Ocean County, Passaic County or Paterson. The mean commute is 36.1 minutes. Routes 9, 18, 34 and 35 cross the township, and the Garden State Parkway crosses the township with Interchange 120 signed for Laurence Harbor and Matawan.

sections.h2: How did Old Bridge grow, and why does it matter for houses?
sections.html:
Old Bridge was mostly farms in its early decades. The population was 1,662 in 1880 and 7,365 in 1950, then tripled to 22,772 by 1960 as farms gave way to subdivisions. The 1980 Census counted 51,406 people, and the extension of Route 18 to the shore brought major change. Lenape people were the first inhabitants, and the Cottrell homestead, built in 1831, still stands at County Route 516 and Cottrell Road.

The growth between 1950 and 1980 shaped most of the township's neighborhoods. Old Bridge's climate is now classed as humid subtropical, so summer humidity and heavy rain are part of the maintenance picture for roofs, siding and crawl spaces. Low ground near Raritan Bay and the creeks needs a closer look at drainage when you prepare a house for showings.

sections.h2: When are Old Bridge property taxes due?
sections.html:
State law sets four installments, mailed ahead of each due date. A grace period of ten days is optional and set by township resolution, and the statutory ceiling on late interest is 8% a year up to $1,500 and 18% above.

Statutory installment mailing and due dates used by New Jersey tax collectors
InstallmentLatest mailing dateDue date
FirstDecember 31February 1
SecondMarch 31May 1
ThirdJune 14August 1
FourthSeptember 30November 1

A bill that goes out late must give at least 25 days to pay, and interest then runs from the original due date. Old Bridge's fourth quarter bills in 2025 prompted a township statement because the third quarter had been estimated on a 4.79% rise while the final 2025 increase came in near 10%.

sections.h2: Why did Old Bridge tax bills jump in 2025?
sections.html:
The township explained in August 2025 that school tax makes up about 60% of the total property tax bill. The school levy rose 13.87% that year, while the municipal tax rate rose 1.58%. The final 2025 and preliminary 2026 bill went out in late August or early September, and the township pointed owners to the Board of Education at 732-566-1000 for school budget questions.

A third quarter estimate can understate the year, and the fourth quarter then carries the catch-up. Pull the full year's billed and paid amounts from the collector before choosing a closing date, and have the closing agent prorate against the actual bill rather than the estimate.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an Old Bridge assessment?
sections.html:
Owners file with the Middlesex County Board of Taxation, 75 Bayard Street, 4th Floor, New Brunswick, phone 732-745-3350. Petitions can be filed online through an account. Evidence may go up with the petition or as late as seven calendar days before the hearing, by 4:00 p.m., and the system routes the petition to the board, the assessor and the clerk. The board resolved that it will not hold virtual hearings. Its office, which serves twenty-five municipalities, is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:15 p.m.

  • A regular petition has an April 1 cutoff, moved to May 1 if the township revalued or reassessed.
  • Added and omitted assessment appeals are due December 1, and the county must receive them, not just see a postmark
  • You must be current on taxes through the first quarter of the tax year to proceed.
  • Appeals cover value only, never the tax rate set by the budgets.

Owners unhappy with the board's judgment have 45 days from mailing to go to the state Tax Court, and an assessment over $1,000,000 may start there.

sections.h2: Which relief programs apply to Old Bridge owners?
sections.html:
The state's ANCHOR program gives property tax relief to New Jersey owners and renters who live in the property as a main home and meet income limits. One combined form covers Senior Freeze, ANCHOR and Stay NJ; the 2025 form was due November 2, 2026.

With 17.8% of residents 65 or older in Old Bridge, several programs are worth a look.

  • Senior Freeze reimburses increases in tax on a main home.
  • ANCHOR covers owners and renters under the income limits.
  • Local deductions for veterans, seniors and disabled owners come from the township assessor.

sections.h2: What should an Old Bridge seller check before listing?
sections.html:
The township directory lists a Rent Stabilization Board, a Building and Code department and a Zoning Board, so landlords and anyone with an unfinished project should check each office before a sale. Ask the building department whether permits for a deck, basement or addition are closed, and ask the assessor whether an added assessment is pending.

Deed filing happens at the Middlesex County Clerk, whose office can give the current fee schedule. The collector can issue a payoff letter good through the closing date. All of Old Bridge Township lies within the Old Bridge school district, so school boundaries are the same across the township.

faqs.q: Who do I call about Old Bridge property tax?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Collector's office at (732) 721-5600, extension 2999. It bills and collects the tax, and the Tax Assessor handles valuation.

faqs.q: Where do Old Bridge assessment appeals go?
faqs.a: They go to the Middlesex County Board of Taxation in New Brunswick, which takes petitions through an online portal. April 1 is the regular cutoff, and May 1 follows a revaluation.

faqs.q: What share of an Old Bridge tax bill is school tax?
faqs.a: About 60% in 2025, according to the township. That year the school levy rose 13.87% and the municipal rate rose 1.58%.

faqs.q: Can I pay Old Bridge property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes. The township's online system accepts payments from a bank account or card, and nominal processing fees apply. Owners need a web login ID, which is printed on the tax bill.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Old Bridge house with tax owing?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing agent pays the collector out of the seller's proceeds, using a written payoff figure that is good for the closing date.
